title: Squarefree Order Kills Multiplicities
content: `factorization_eq_one_of_squarefree_dvd`: if |G| is squarefree and a prime p divides it, then the p-adic valuation v_p(|G|) is exactly 1. This is a direct application of Mathlib's `Nat.factorization_eq_one_of_squarefree`. It is the single number-theoretic engine of the whole entry: a squarefree number has no repeated prime factor, so every multiplicity is at most one, and divisibility forces it to be exactly one. The Group/Finite instances are omitted here because the statement is purely about the natural number |G|.
mathContext: $\mathrm{Squarefree}\,|G| \wedge p \mid |G| \implies v_p(|G|) = 1$ — no prime appears above the first power.

title: Sylow Subgroups Have Prime Order
content: `sylow_card_eq_prime_of_squarefree`: if |G| is squarefree and p ∣ |G|, then every Sylow p-subgroup P has order exactly p. The proof composes the parent entry's `Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity` (|P| = p^(v_p|G|)) with the multiplicity collapse v_p|G| = 1 and rewrites p¹ = p (`pow_one`). The 'merely large p-subgroup' of the general Sylow theory becomes a group of prime order — a single equality with no case analysis.

title: Cyclic of Prime Order
content: `sylow_isCyclic_of_squarefree_dvd`: under squarefreeness, every Sylow p-subgroup with p ∣ |G| is cyclic. It has prime order p (previous lemma), and a finite group of prime order is cyclic (`isCyclic_of_prime_card`), so P ≅ ℤ/pℤ. This is the literal statement the parent entry's open question requested: |G| squarefree ⟹ every Sylow subgroup cyclic of prime order.
mathContext: $|P| = p \implies P \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ — prime order forces cyclic.

title: The Sharp Order Dichotomy
content: `sylow_card_eq_one_or_prime_of_squarefree`: under squarefreeness, a Sylow p-subgroup has order 1 (precisely when p ∤ |G|) or p (precisely when p ∣ |G|) — never a higher power. A case split on p ∣ |G| uses the prime-order lemma in one branch and `Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_dvd` (giving |P| = p^0 = 1) in the other. This makes the parent's `sylow_nontrivial_iff_dvd` boundary razor sharp: the only nontrivial possibility is prime order.
mathContext: $|P| \in \{1, p\}$ for every prime $p$ — order 1 iff $p \nmid |G|$, order $p$ iff $p \mid |G|$.

title: Every Sylow Subgroup Is Cyclic
content: `sylow_isCyclic_of_squarefree`: with no hypothesis on p, every Sylow p-subgroup of a squarefree-order group is cyclic. When p ∣ |G| it is cyclic of prime order (previous lemma); when p ∤ |G| it is trivial (order 1, a subsingleton) and hence cyclic by `isCyclic_of_subsingleton`. So the dichotomy 'order 1 or p' upgrades to the uniform statement that the whole Sylow data of a squarefree-order group consists of cyclic groups.

title: Packaged: Cyclic of Prime Order
content: `sylow_cyclic_of_prime_order_of_squarefree`: the complete packaged answer — if |G| is squarefree and p ∣ |G|, then every Sylow p-subgroup is simultaneously of order exactly p and cyclic. This conjunction is the form a working group theorist cites, and it is the witness used by the S₃ specializations below.

title: |S₃| = 6 Is Squarefree
content: `squarefree_card_perm_fin3`: the order of S₃ is 6 = 2·3, which is squarefree. Proved by rewriting via the parent's `card_perm_fin3`, factoring 6 = 2·3, and applying `Nat.squarefree_mul_iff` with the coprimality of 2 and 3 and `Prime.squarefree` for each factor. This unlocks the general theorem for the symmetric group on three letters. (Kernel `decide` does not reduce `Squarefree`, so the structural lemma is used instead, keeping the file 0-axiom.)

title: Sylow 2-Subgroup of S₃: Cyclic of Order 2
content: `sylow2_perm_fin3_cyclic`: every Sylow 2-subgroup of S₃ is cyclic of order 2 — recovered as an instance of `sylow_cyclic_of_prime_order_of_squarefree` applied to |S₃| = 6 at p = 2. The parent entry's concrete number 2 is now a corollary of the uniform squarefree theorem rather than a standalone computation.
mathContext: $P \in \mathrm{Syl}_2(S_3) \implies |P| = 2 \wedge \mathrm{IsCyclic}\,P$ — the order-2 subgroup generated by a transposition.

title: Sylow 3-Subgroup of S₃: Cyclic of Order 3
content: `sylow3_perm_fin3_cyclic`: every Sylow 3-subgroup of S₃ is cyclic of order 3 — the alternating group A₃ of 3-cycles — recovered as an instance of `sylow_cyclic_of_prime_order_of_squarefree` at p = 3. Together with the order-2 case this reproduces the parent's full S₃ Sylow picture as specializations of the general theorem, exactly as the open question requested.
